 Dynamic and Fatigue Testing Systems
 Products
»
 Testing Systems
»
 Dynamic and Fatigue Testing Systems
Instron offers an extensive range of fully-integrated dynamic and fatigue testing systems from 1000 N up to 5000 kN. Incorporating servohydraulic, servo-electric, and linear motor technologies, these test instruments cover a broad range of fatigue, dynamic, and static testing applications, including high-cycle fatigue, low-cycle fatigue, thermo-mechanical fatigue, fracture mechanics, crack propagation and growth studies, fracture toughness, bi-axial, axial-torsional, multi-axial, high strain rate, quasi-static, creep, stress-relaxation, and other types of dynamic and static tests.
 ElectroPuls® All-Electric Dynamic and Fatigue Test Systems
Linear electric motor-driven dynamic test machines built for fatigue and fracture mechanics testing, offering a clean, quiet, plug-and-play alternative to traditional hydraulic systems.
Learn More 
 General Purpose Hydraulic Fatigue
General purpose servohydraulic systems ideal for high-cycle and low-cycle fatigue, fracture mechanics, and quasi-static testing across a wide range of materials and components.
Learn More 
 Low Strain Rate 8862 Servo-Electric Systems
8862 Electric Actuator Systems are uniquely designed for the low strain rate requirements of LCF testing, using electric technology to minimize infrastructure requirements and running costs.
Learn More 
 High Strain Rate VHS Systems
High-Strain Rate VHS systems characterize strain rate-dependent materials, such as automotive crash structures, at test speeds of up to 25 m/s.
Learn More 
 Axial-Torsion 8850 Systems
Axial-torsion 8850 series systems support static and fatigue testing with combined axial and torsional loading of up to 2000 Nm and 250 kN.
Learn More 
 ElectroPuls 16-Station Testing Systems
The ElectroPuls 16-station fatigue fixture allows simultaneous testing of up to 16 specimens, significantly reducing total test times and improving overall testing efficiency. This high-capacity setup helps laboratories accelerate development cycles and deliver new products to market even sooner.
Learn More 
 Biaxial Cruciform Test Systems
Planar biaxial cruciform systems use four in-plane actuators and advanced control software to perform precise two-axis tensile, fatigue, and fracture testing with synchronized multi-axis control.
Learn More 
 8800MT Controller / Controller Upgrades
Controller upgrades are a great way to give existing hydraulic equipment a new lease on life, bringing the benefits of modern electronics and software to your laboratory without the cost of a full system replacement.
Learn More 
 High Temperature Fatigue
High temperature fatigue testing includes low cycle fatigue (LCF), thermomechanical fatigue (TMF), and electro-thermal mechanical testing (ETMT) — all essential for evaluating material performance under extreme thermal and mechanical conditions.
Learn More 
 Out of Production Dynamic Systems
Systems that are no longer in production still receive a comprehensive level of ongoing technical and replacement part support. View this section to understand where your system stands in its product life cycle and consider which options exist to upgrade or retrofit your existing equipment.
Learn More 
 Talk to an Instron Expert.
Not sure which dynamic or fatigue testing system fits your application? Tell us about your testing requirements and we will help you find the right solution.

Testing Accessories
 Products
»
 Testing Accessories
Leveraging deep applications experience and engineering expertise, Instron provides a comprehensive range of accessories for materials testing systems. Our portfolio includes hundreds of grips, fixtures, load cells, and application‑specific solutions engineered to support accurate, repeatable testing across a wide variety of materials and standards. Pair these accessories with our testing software for full control over test setup, execution, and analysis. Choose a category below, view the interactive accessories catalog(opens in new tab), or download a PDF version(opens in new tab) to get started.
 Load Cells
Load cells convert the force experienced by the specimen into an electrical signal used by the electronic controller to precisely monitor, report, and control the applied force. Instron designs and manufactures its own load cells — ensuring accuracy, compatibility, and traceability across the full range of Instron testing systems.
Learn More 
 Extensometers
Extensometry provides a direct and accurate method for measuring and controlling specimen deformation by monitoring strain over a precisely defined gauge length. Instron offers contacting and non-contacting extensometers for static, dynamic, and high-temperature applications.
Learn More 
 Chambers and Furnaces
Environmental chambers and furnaces provide the capability to study the mechanical properties of materials and components across a wide temperature range — from sub-zero cryogenic conditions through to +1,600°C — for applications where temperature has a critical influence on material behavior.
Learn More 
 Tensile Grips
A wide range of tensile grip styles and force capacities for holding diverse materials including thread, rope, rubber, plastics, composites, fasteners, sheet metal, and more. Each grip type is engineered for secure, consistent specimen clamping to minimize slippage and ensure accurate results.
Learn More 
 Compression Platens
Compression platens and anvils in a range of sizes and force capacities — from rigid foam and packaging materials through to concrete cylinders, cubes, and high-strength structural specimens.
Learn More 
 Flex Fixtures
Three and four-point bend fixtures for determining the stiffness, yield, and flexural strength of plastics, metals, composites, and similar rigid materials to ASTM, ISO, and EN standards.
Learn More 
 Peel, Friction, Puncture
Fixtures for performing peel, puncture, burst, and coefficient of friction tests on adhesives, films, foils, packaging, and coated materials to a wide range of industry standards.
Learn More 
 Torsion Add-On
The Torsion Add-On 3.0 can be installed on any new or existing 6800 or 5900 Series universal testing system to enable simultaneous axial and torsional testing of components such as bone screws, Luer locks, electrical knobs, and more.
Learn More 
 AT2 Automated XY Stage
The AT2 can be added to any new or existing 6800 or 5900 Series system to automate compression, tensile, and flexure testing of devices or components with multiple test points or repetitive test locations — widely used in biomedical and electronics testing.
Learn More 
 Frame Accessories
Load frame accessories designed to fit specific Instron testing frames — including support tables, protective debris shields, T-slot tables, in-head wedge grips, in-head tension rods, and more.
Learn More 
 Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Fixtures
Fixtures and accessories for testing medical devices, drug delivery systems, surgical instruments, implants, and pharmaceutical packaging — supporting compliance with ISO, ASTM, and regulatory requirements for biomedical and healthcare applications.
Learn More 
 Electronics and Microelectronics Fixtures
Grips, fixtures, and system add-ons for tension, compression, flexure, peel, shear, and puncture testing of electronic components, PCBs, connectors, and microelectronic devices.
Learn More 
 Battery Testing Solutions
Accessories for testing the mechanical properties of materials, adhesives, welds, and components found in battery cells, modules, and packs — supporting the development and quality control of battery systems for electric vehicles, consumer electronics, and energy storage applications.
Learn More 
 Composite Fixtures
Fixtures for tension, compression, flexure, shear, and peel testing of composite materials — most designed to meet specific ASTM, ISO, and EN composite testing standards.
Learn More 
 Couplings and Adapters
Couplings and adapters modify the test system's connection type, allowing you to interface with a wider range of grips and fixtures across different clevis, threaded, and flanged connection types.
Learn More 
 Fastener Fixtures
Fixtures designed for fast and accurate tensile testing of bolts, screws, studs, and nuts — including proof load, wedge tensile, and cone stripping test configurations to ASTM F606 and related standards.
Learn More 
 Test Plates
T-slot tables and component test plates for mounting or clamping components, structures, and assemblies for tensile, compression, bend, peel, and puncture testing.
Learn More 
 Food Testing Fixtures
Fixtures covering a wide range of industry-standard food texture testing methods — including compression, puncture, shear, and extrusion tests for evaluating the texture, firmness, and consistency of food products.
Learn More 
 Wood Fixtures
Fixtures for testing wood and wood-based products for adhesive bond strength, compression, bend strength, shear, and tensile strength to standard and application-specific test methods.
Learn More 
 Crash Simulation Accessories
Accessories for low-speed rear, side, and pole impact simulation — supporting the development and validation of automotive safety systems with improved productivity and testing efficiency.
Learn More 
 Alignment Fixtures
Fixtures and software for measuring and adjusting load string alignment in real time — essential for applications where testing standards specify alignment requirements, such as Nadcap and ISO 23788.
Learn More 
 Specimen Measuring and Preparation
Solutions for specimen cutting, marking, and dimensional measurement — ensuring correct specimen geometry and consistency for accurate and repeatable test results.
Learn More 
 Out of Production Accessories
A listing of major accessories for Instron testing systems that are no longer in production — including environmental chambers, extensometers, tensile grips, and hydraulic grip pumps — with information on available alternatives and upgrade paths.
Learn More 
 Out of Production Specimen Preparation and Measuring Devices
A listing of notching machines, punching machines, and other specimen preparation devices that are no longer in production, with guidance on available alternatives.
Learn More

Not finding the accessory you need? Instron has developed thousands of custom grips, fixtures, and accessories — many of which are not listed in our standard catalog. Tell us about your application and we will help you find the right solution.

»
 Test Types
»
 Dynamic Fatigue Testing
 Dynamic Fatigue Testing
 An Introduction
A dynamic testing machine performs repeated loading mechanical testing. Where a tensile testing machine would apply a quasi-static load to measure the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength until the specimen reaches its break or rupture point, a dynamic testing machine usually stresses a material within its elastic region with cyclic loads until the specimen fails due to fatigue. The typical types of testing include high cycle fatigue, low cycle fatigue, fracture mechanics including pre-cracking, thermo-mechanical fatigue, and simulated tests such as athletic footwear, auto-injectors or stents. Dynamic testing machines utilize various technologies including servo hydraulic actuators, servo electric motors and linear electric motors.
 Dynamic Testing Machine
 Components and Parts
Fatigue tests are performed on dynamic testing machines. A dynamic testing machine consists of a test frame that is equipped with a load cell, testing software, and application-specific grips and accessories, such as extensometers. The type of material being tested will determine the type of accessories needed, and a single machine can be adapted to test any material within its force range by simply changing the fixturing.
Dynamic Testing Machine
Load Frame
Dynamic testing machine load frames can come as either Servo-hydraulic, Servo-electric or Linear-Electric depending on their force capacity and dynamic performance.
Software
Test software is where operators can setup the machine, create test methods, run the test and export the results.
Load Cell
The load cell is a transducer that measures the force applied to the test specimen. Instron’s patented Dynacell’s also incorporate accelerometers to remove the errors in load introduced by inertia from high speed dynamic testing.
Grips and Fixtures
A wide range of specimen grips and fixtures are available for specimens of different materials, shapes, and sizes.
Strain Measurement
Some test methods require measurement of a specimen’s elongation under load. Instron supplies several contacting and non-contacting devices suitable for dynamic strain measurement and control.
Dynamic testing machines are available in a variety of different sizes, force capacities ranging from 1000 N to 5 MN, and dynamic performance from 1 Hz to 100 Hz. Most low force dynamic testing is performed on a linear electric motor machine, while higher force applications require Servohydraulic frames and actuators. Instron's ElectroPuls systems are available in capacity ranges from 1000 N to 20 kN and can perform a wide range of different test types, including tension-tension, tension-compression, compression-compression, bend fatigue, and a wide array of biomedical standards. Instron’s Servohydraulic systems are designed for higher capacity testing from 25 kN to 5 MN for testing stronger materials and larger components such as high strength steels and advanced composites.
 Dynamic Testing Standards
 Standards for Testing Plastics, Elastomers, and Metals
Most dynamic testing is performed on established standards published by standards organisations such as ASTM and ISO. Testing standards prescribe acceptable test parameters and results for different types of raw materials such as metals, plastics, elastomers, textiles, and composites, as well as for finished products such as medical devices, automotive parts and consumer electronics. These standards ensure that materials and products entering the supply chain display predictable mechanical properties and are not likely to fail in their expected end use. Since the cost and safety implications of product failure cannot be overstated, companies and encouraged to invest in high-quality, accurate testing equipment that is designed to help them easily determine whether or not their products meet applicable standards.
ASTM E647 / E399 / E1820
Bluehill Fracture modules support all common test standards (ASTM, ISO and BS) for crack propagation, ductile and brittle fracture, crack length measurements and specimen geometries. Users can test to predefined standards (e.g. ASTM E647, ASTM E399, ASTM E1820, ISO 12135).
ISO 14801
With an array of implant sizes and geometries, angled dental implants can be mounted into a variable angle fixture for testing to the ISO 14801 standard. The fixture needs to ensure that the mounting does not over constraint the implant nor generate large lateral forces that can damage the load cell or the testing machine. Pre-angled dental implants should be tested in ambient air using a frequency of 15 Hz.
ASTM F1717
The Instron spinal fixture is designed to meet ASTM F1717-12 requirements. In accordance with the standard, the UHMWPE blocks are attached to the spinal fixture. The design of the blocks can differ, according to the clinical application at the intended spinal location. The way that the blocks are connected to the fixture allow a degree of freedom when performing bending compression, bending tensile, and torsional testing.
 Tuning
 Less Setup, More Testing
Stiffness Based Tuning is a revolutionary method of tuning your fatigue testing system, which improves your machine usability and helps to improve your data accuracy. The new process is simple for all users, and without pre-cycling the specimen it helps to make your data more reliable and repeatable.
Quicker Process
Over 75% time saving by using patented tuning technique
More Accessible
Simple process builds user confidence and reduces reliance on experts
No Pre-Cycling
No specimen damage before the start of your test
Improved Accuracy
Perfectly tuned system helps to ensure reliable data and accurate peaks
